method: Author independently opened each manifest-bound original PNG once, before constructing either FigureSpec. No answer files or existing modern figures were used.

groups.observation: One horizontal, thick hatched boundary band spans almost the whole image. One straight vertical normal passes through its central incidence location and extends into both media. The upper region is the first medium; the lower region is the second. Neither medium has a printed name or index.

The upper-right oblique ray points down-left toward the boundary intersection. The lower-left oblique ray points down-left away from that same intersection. The lower ray is closer to the downward normal than the upper ray is to the upward normal. There is no reflected ray, apparatus, third branch, or numerical angle.

The alpha symbol and short upper arc occupy the wedge between the upward normal and incident ray. The beta symbol and short lower arc occupy the wedge between the downward normal and refracted ray. Both are measured from the normal, not the horizontal boundary.

modernAdditions: English Medium 1, Medium 2, Incident, Refracted, Normal and Boundary labels; O identifies the existing unlabelled incidence location.
Semantic-role lower-region fill replaces the source boundary hatching as a medium distinction; hatching is not a measured lattice.
Small endpoint/construction markers and exact coordinates are modern layout choices, not recovered pixel measurements or given data.
Normal is dashed to distinguish it from light. Alpha and beta are preserved as mathematical symbols. No reflected branch is added to Figure 153.

routing.reason: Source consists entirely of a planar boundary, normal, directed rays, and angle markers. Existing JSXGraph objects express every necessary relation.

groups.observation: One unlabelled rectangular transparent aquarium is drawn as a wireframe perspective box. A wide front face, narrower receding right face, rear/top rim, vertical uprights and bottom edges are visible. Rear upper rim is higher and shifted right relative to the front upper rim. No lamp, projector, screen, fish, smoke cloud, measuring disk, or labelled parts are depicted.

The lower part of the front and right faces contains irregular horizontal and perspective hatch strokes. A horizontal water/air edge crosses the front face around mid-height; the right/rear surface edge recedes upward-right in the drawing. Empty space is above the water inside the tank. These hatch strokes depict water, not a calibrated grid or equal intervals.

A narrow oblique light trace enters from the upper-right, crosses the upper tank rim, reaches the water surface near the middle of the front width, and continues down-left as a more nearly vertical bright gap/trace in the water hatching. A second dashed trace is adjacent to the upper diagonal trace. Its pixels do not establish a separate upper-left reflected branch; it must not be called a source reflected ray. No arrowheads, normal, Greek labels, numerical angles, material indices, or calibrated beam widths are printed.

modernAdditions: Air, Water, Aquarium, Incident, Refracted, Reflected and Normal labels are modern English instructional labels, not printed source labels. Water identity and fluorescence are bound to already-reviewed EN/ZH prose.

An explicitly modern dashed reflected direction goes upper-left from the shared incidence point; it is supported by the full reviewed lesson's discussion of reflection, not claimed as a resolved source branch.
A dashed normal through the water entry and O identifier are modern construction aids. Their geometry is exact and no angle is measured from the horizontal boundary.
Role-colored water fill replaces non-calibrated historical hatching, and a light band retains the visible submerged path. Color is not a wavelength, intensity or fluorescence measurement.
Coordinates, beam width, projection proportions, small endpoint markers and illustrative angles are regularized schematic choices, not source measurements. No light-source hardware is invented.

routing.reason: Actual source pixels depict a geometric wireframe aquarium and ray-path demonstration, not a photographic/natural scene or object-specific optical hardware. A rectangular-prism schematic, surface polygons and exact light directions are native JSXGraph geometry. No semantic artwork layer is necessary to retain the depicted apparatus.
